==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|īʹd(ə)l}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈaɪd(ə)l/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈʌɪdəl/|a=CA,idle-idol split}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-idle.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪdəl|s=2}}
* {{homophones|en|idol|idyll|idyl}} {{qualifier|US pronunciation}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|idel}}, {{m|enm|ydel}}, from {{inh|en|ang|īdel}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*īdl}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*īdlaz}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|ijdel|t=vain, meaningless}}, {{m|nl|ijl||rareified, skinny}}, {{m|nl|iel||thin, slender}}; {{cog|nds-de|iedel|t=vain, idle}}; {{cog|de|eitel|t=vain, conceited}}; and possibly {{cog|non|illr}} {{gloss|"bad"; > {{cog|en|ill}}}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[empty|Empty]], [[vacant]].
#: {{syn|en|bare|leer|void}}
# Not being used appropriately; not [[occupy|occupied]]; (of time) with no, no important, or not much activity.
#: {{syn|en|dormant|quiescent|suspended|Thesaurus:inactive}}
#: {{ux|en|'''idle''' hours}}
#: {{ux|en|My computer [[hibernate]]s after it has been '''idle''' for 30 minutes.}}
# Not engaged in any [[occupation]] or [[employment]]; [[unemployed]]; [[inactive]]; doing nothing in particular.
#: {{syn|en|unbusied|workless|Thesaurus:obsolete|Thesaurus:unemployed}}
#: {{ux|en|'''idle''' workmen}}
#* {{RQ:Jefferies Amateur Poacher|chapter=1|passage=Molly the dairymaid came a little way from the rickyard, and said she would pluck the pigeon that very night after work. She was always ready to do anything for us boys; and we could never quite make out why they scolded her so for an '''idle''' hussy indoors. It seemed so unjust. Looking back, I recollect she had very beautiful brown eyes.}}
# [[averse|Averse]] to [[work]], [[labor]] or [[employment]]; [[lazy]]; [[slothful]].
#: {{syn|en|indolent|inert|Thesaurus:lazy}}
#: {{ux|en|an '''idle''' fellow}}
#* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|VI|passage=“I don't mean all of your friends—only a small proportion—which, however, connects your circle with that deadly, '''idle''', brainless bunch—the insolent chatterers at the opera, the gorged dowagers, the worn-out, passionless men, the enervated matrons of the summer capital,{{nb...}}!”}}
# Of no [[importance]]; [[useless]]; [[worthless]]; [[vain]]; [[trifling]]; [[thoughtless]]; [[silly]].
#: {{syn|en|petty|pointless|Thesaurus:insignificant}}
#: {{ux|en|an '''idle''' story;  '''idle''' talk;  '''idle''' rumor;  '''idle''' threats;  '''idle''' pleasures}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Light-headed; foolish.
#: {{syn|en|fatuous|unwise|Thesaurus:foolish}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1628|author={{w|John Ford (dramatist)|John Ford}}|title=w:The Lover's Melancholy
|passage=The youth is '''idle'''}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|idelen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|īdlian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*īdlēn}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|eiteln|t=to make empty, free up}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To spend (time) in [[idleness]]; to [[waste]]; to [[consume]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1912|author=Frederick Arthur Talbot|title=Making Good in Canada|page=81
|text={{...}} the ne'er-do-anything-at-home who '''idled''' his day in immaculate attire and who was banished to Canada on a "remittance," shares his pork and beans with the sourdough, who has scratched rocks and sifted black sand from his infancy.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1920|author=Raine Bennett|title=After the Day: A Collection of Post-war Impressions|page=1
|text=While '''idling''' the hours I trace verses / On the inside of wrappers embellishing cans Of Bordeaux mackerel, caught in Monterey.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1967|title=Urner Field Observer|page=49
|text=he {{...}} lay in his blind '''idling''' the hours until the rising tide would send the shorebirds in across the marsh. Not far off two sons of Southern Italy were lazily transferring a stack of cut salt hay to a one horse hay cart.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2017-09-01|author=Angela King|title=The Blood of Kings|publisher=Open Road Media|isbn=9781504070867
|text='If I know William, he'll be settled in some airy corridor, '''idling''' the hours until he can ride in comfort.' }}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[lose]] or [[spend]] [[time]] doing nothing, or without being [[employed]] in [[business]].
#: {{ux|en|to '''idle''' in an [[IRC]] channel}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1939|author=Joan Evans|title=Chateaubriand|page=32
|passage=He had already heard of the young man's projected journey — evidently the Comte de Combourg had written many letters while his son '''idled''' at St. Malo {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of an engine: to [[run]] at a slow [[speed]], or out of [[gear]]; to [[tick over]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause (an engine) to idle (run at a slow speed, or out of gear).
#: {{ux|en|The driver '''idle'''d his engine until the car finally stalled.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|chiefly|of a layoff or a labor strike}} To make (workers, students, etc) idle; to leave without work.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# The state of [[#Verb|idling]], of being [[#Adjective|idle]].
# {{lb|en|mechanical engineering}} The lowest selectable [[thrust]] or [[power]] [[setting]] of an [[engine]].
#: {{syn|en|full throttle|wide open}}
#: {{coi|en|a lumpy '''idle'''}}<!--denotes how the idle sounds, in engines tuned for high-end performance-->
#: {{ux|en|A slight valve tap was audible at '''idle''' but was not noticeable otherwise.}}
